@copilot Update this PR directly on `open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation` branch `copilot/trask-update-benchmark`. Keep the branch assigned by GitHub Copilot. Do not rename it or create a replacement branch or PR as a workaround. If GitHub assigns a follow-up branch, keep that branch.

Measure the same thing for Petclinic and Spring smoke: JVM uptime sampled inside the application while producing the first successful readiness response. Keep smoke's `/greeting` behavior and `X-Startup-JVM-Uptime-Millis` header. For Petclinic, read the same header on the first HTTP 200 for `GET /petclinic/api/owners/1` whose body passes the existing seeded PostgreSQL owner validation. Keep the existing readiness probing cadence. Fail clearly if the validated response lacks a positive integer uptime rather than falling back to another clock. Remove the Docker `StartedAt` and host-clock subtraction from timing samples. Do not use Spring log or Actuator timing. Keep JFR profiling separate from the measured samples.

Layer a small benchmark-only helper JAR onto the pinned Petclinic image, without rebuilding the image or adding a second Java agent. Build the helper for Java 17 against Petclinic's Spring Boot 2.4.2 / Spring MVC dependencies without bundling Spring. Register a `ResponseBodyAdvice` using Boot 2.4 auto-configuration via `META-INF/spring.factories`. Scope it to the seeded-owner GET and set the header from `ManagementFactory.getRuntimeMXBean().getUptime()` after the controller returns and before Spring writes the response body, without changing that body. Load the helper via the existing `PropertiesLauncher` mechanism alongside the annotations JAR for every Petclinic configuration, including the no-agent control and profile launches. Do not add the helper to any published artifact or require it for smoke.

Wire the helper into the standalone benchmark and the build and measurement artifact flow in `.github/workflows/agent-startup-benchmark.yml`. Keep smoke as the default. Update the benchmark README, report, and timing metadata to describe the common metric: uptime at the successful probe response, including agent initialization and application/request work before the sample, excluding container setup, database provisioning, and return network transit. Poll timing can still affect when the successful probe reaches the app. Add focused coverage of the Petclinic response/header handling and run relevant tests, including a short Petclinic benchmark if Docker is available.

replies.body: Updated in e1170ab9. Both workloads now use application JVM uptime, and Petclinic loads the benchmark-only advice through `PropertiesLauncher`. The focused tests and a short Petclinic run, including its separate JFR launch, passed.

@copilot Apply the three simplifications below directly to open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation#21413 on its existing head, `open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation:copilot/trask-update-benchmark`. Keep the branch GitHub Copilot assigned. Do not rename or replace it or open a separate PR as a workaround. Keep any follow-up branch GitHub assigns.

1. In `benchmark-overhead`'s `PetclinicStartupUptimeResponseAdvice`, add `X-Startup-JVM-Version` from `System.getProperty("java.runtime.version")` on the same readiness response that already carries `X-Startup-JVM-Uptime-Millis`, matching smoke's `WebController`. In `AgentStartupBenchmark`, return the parsed positive uptime and nonblank JVM version from `awaitReadiness` so `sample` uses that result instead of parsing uptime again or running `java -version` inside Petclinic after every launch. Keep the existing successful-status and body checks, error behavior, and polling cadence. Do not issue another HTTP request or move the in-app timing boundary or separate JFR cutoff.

2. Have Boot 2.4.2 import `PetclinicStartupUptimeResponseAdvice` directly through `src/startupHelper/resources/META-INF/spring.factories`. Keep `@ControllerAdvice` and put `@Configuration(proxyBeanMethods = false)` on the same class. Delete the `PetclinicStartupUptimeAutoConfiguration` bean wrapper and update the helper JAR validation for the single class and registration resource. The advice still applies only to `GET /petclinic/api/owners/1` and must preserve the response body.

3. Compile the Petclinic helper once in the standalone `benchmark-overhead/build.gradle.kts`. Put its Java source in `src/startupHelper/java` alongside its resources, configure that source set for Java 17, and use its compiled output both in the tests and in `petclinic-startup-helper.jar`. Remove the custom per-file compile list and the unused standalone `spring-boot-autoconfigure` dependency. The pinned Spring MVC 5.3.3 dependency supplies the APIs, and Boot stays in the Petclinic image. Do not bundle Spring. Keep the existing JAR/task names, prebuilt helper override, and workflow artifact/checksum flow intact.

Preserve the pinned images and PostgreSQL seeded-owner check, smoke as the default, the same Petclinic helper and annotations classpath for all agent configurations, and the separate startup recorder for JFR. Update the benchmark README only where its helper build description becomes stale. From `benchmark-overhead`, run the narrow checks (`./gradlew spotlessApply test --tests 'io.opentelemetry.startup.*Test' startupRecorderJar petclinicStartupHelperJar`). Verify the JAR contains the advice and registration resource and targets Java 17. If Docker is available, check the wiring with a short Petclinic run.

replies.body: Applied the requested updates in `dd212894`. The focused Gradle checks and a short Petclinic run passed; the helper JAR contains the advice and registration resource and targets Java 17.
